extracted.intended_audience: U.S. importers, exporters, and reexporters of endangered terrestrial plants; other affected entities; public commenters; APHIS/agency stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Notice requesting revision and extension of OMB approval for APHIS information collection under the Endangered Species Act and forfeiture procedures (7 CFR parts 355 and 356), and soliciting public comments on necessity, burden, clarity, and minimizing respondent burden. Covers permit application requirements, required recordkeeping/reporting, and forfeiture-related submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain a protected plant permit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any entity wishing to engage in the business of importing, exporting, or reexporting terrestrial plants listed in the CITES regulations at 50 CFR 17.12 or 23.23 must obtain a protected plant permit from APHIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to entities who sell, barter, collect, or otherwise exchange or acquire terrestrial plants as a livelihood or enterprise engaged in for gain or profit. The requirement does not apply to persons engaged in business merely as carriers or customhouse brokers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of entities 'engaged in the business'
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities include importers, exporters, or reexporters who sell, barter, collect, or otherwise exchange or acquire terrestrial plants as a livelihood or enterprise engaged in for gain or profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of who must obtain permits; carriers and customhouse brokers are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit application and submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a protected plant permit, entities must complete an application and submit it to APHIS for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a permit has been issued, the plants covered by the permit may be imported into the United States, exported, or reexported, provided they are accompanied by documentation required by the regulations and all other conditions of the regulations are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of permit denial (information collection activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include appealing the denial of a permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are part of the collection and recordkeeping framework that APHIS administers under these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking containers used for import/export/reexport
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include marking containers used for the importation, exportation, or reexportation of the plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking is a required operational step tied to compliance and documentation; the notice lists it among the collection activities APHIS uses to regulate trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying APHIS of impending import/export/reexport
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include notifying APHIS of the impending importation, exportation, or reexportation of the plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice to APHIS enables monitoring and enforcement and is part of the regulatory information collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include validating documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document validation is an APHIS information-collection step to ensure required documentation accompanies shipments as regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating and maintaining records of import/export/reexport
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include creating and maintaining records of importation, exportation, and reexportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping is required to support enforcement, reporting, and potential investigations of violations under the Endangered Species Act and the Lacey Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting related reports from required records
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities include submitting related reports from records required to be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting based on maintained records feeds into APHIS monitoring and compliance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture procedures filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities whose property is subject to forfeiture may file with APHIS a waiver of forfeiture procedures, a claim, a request for return of property, or petition for remission or mitigation of forfeiture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These filings are procedural mechanisms under 7 CFR part 356 that are part of the agency's information collection and adjudicatory processes for forfeited plants or other property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of public comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice solicits comments to: (1) evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Agency, including whether the information will have practical utility; (2) evaluate the accuracy of our estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used; (3) enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (4) minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, through use, as appropriate, of automated, electronic, mechanical, and other collection technologies; e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments should address these four PRA-focused questions to inform the agency's OMB submission and adjustments to the information collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated public burden metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The public burden for this collection of information is estimated to average 0.096 hours per response. Estimated annual number of respondents: 1,097. Estimated annual number of responses per respondent: 137. Estimated annual number of responses: 149,876. Estimated total annual burden on respondents: 14,436 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numerical estimates are provided for commenters to evaluate and, if appropriate, challenge or suggest revisions to burden assumptions and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment reducing burden (PPQ Form 368 moved)
rubrics_metrics.description: APHIS has amended this information collection by decreasing the number of Responses. In addition, Total Burden Hours reported decreased due to APHIS moving the PPQ Form 368 activity to the new Common Form Information Collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative adjustment affects the burden calculations and the scope of this specific information collection submission to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: How and where to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments by either of the following methods: Federal eRulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov) by entering APHIS-2026-0199, or Postal Mail/Commercial Delivery to Docket No. APHIS-2026-0199, Regulatory Analysis and Development, PPD, APHIS, 5601 Sunnyside Ave., #AP760, Beltsville, MD 20705.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting documents and any comments may be viewed at regulations.gov or in APHIS's reading room (Room 1620 of the USDA South Building) during normal hours; contact provided to confirm assistance availability before visiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment handling and public record notice
rubrics_metrics.description: All responses to this notice will be summarized and included in the request for OMB approval. All comments will also become a matter of public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies review submissions and may redact or withhold certain portions; submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments close date
rubrics_metrics.description: We will consider all comments that we receive on or before April 28, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received after this date may not be considered in the agency's PRA submission for this collection.
